wikipedia#0.title: 2013: Norwegian chess grandmaster Magnus Carlsen (pictured) defeated India's Viswanathan Anand to become world chess champion.

wikipedia#1.title: 2005: Elected by delegates in the newly assembled Bundestag four days after a federal election, Angela Merkel became the first female chancellor of Germany.

wikipedia#2.title: 1995: Toy Story, the first feature film created using only computer-generated imagery, was released in theaters in the United States.

wikipedia#3.title: 1988: The B-2 Spirit stealth bomber of the United States Air Force was first displayed in public at Air Force Plant 42 in Palmdale, California.

wikipedia#4.title: 1987: Two television stations in Chicago had their broadcast signals hijacked with footage of an unknown person wearing a Max Headroom mask and costume.

wikipedia#5.title: 1978: The serpent labret with articulated tongue (pictured articulating between positions), considered among the finest Aztec gold objects known to survive, was sold at Sotheby's.

wikipedia#6.title: 1975: Two days after the death of Francisco Franco, Juan Carlos I (pictured) was declared King of Spain according to the law of succession promulgated by Franco.

wikipedia#7.title: 1971: In Britain's worst mountaineering disaster, five teenage students and one of their leaders were found dead from exposure on the Cairngorm Plateau in the Scottish Highlands.

wikipedia#8.title: 1968: The Beatles released their eponymous double album, popularly known as the White Album.

wikipedia#9.title: 1967: The United Nations Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 242 in the aftermath of the Six-Day War between Israel and Egypt, Jordan, and Syria.

wikipedia#10.title: 1963: John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas; hours later, Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson was sworn in as the 36th president of the United States aboard Air Force One.

wikipedia#11.title: 1910: The crews of three Brazilian warships – all commissioned only months before – and several smaller vessels mutinied against perceived "slavery" being practised in the Brazilian Navy.

wikipedia#12.title: 1873: The French steamship Ville du Havre collided with a Scottish iron clipper in the North Atlantic and sank with the loss of 226 lives.

wikipedia#13.title: 1797: The Geisel School of Medicine, the fourth oldest medical school in the United States, was founded by the physician Nathan Smith.

wikipedia#14.title: 1718: The pirate Blackbeard was killed in battle by a boarding party of British sailors off the coast of the Province of North Carolina.

wikipedia#15.title: 1635: Dutch colonial forces on Formosa launched a three-month pacification campaign against Taiwanese indigenous peoples.

wikipedia#16.title: 1574: Juan Fernández, a Spanish explorer, discovered an archipelago that now bears his name off the coast of Chile.

wikipedia#17.title: 1386: Turco-Mongol conqueror Timur captured and sacked the Georgian capital Tbilisi and forced King Bagrat V to convert to Islam.
